title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, and templates
author: Sofia Ramirez
content:
Overview

This document collects and standardizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and processes for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees and contractors. Owners and reviewers are listed at the top; teams should follow the procedures below and escalate to People Ops or Security where noted.

1) Access and permissions

Purpose
- Ensure least-privilege access while enabling productive work.
- Provide a single source of truth for onboarding, role changes, and offboarding.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood systems, cloud accounts, admin consoles, SaaS applications, and on-premise tooling.

Roles & ownership
- People Ops: onboarding/offboarding coordination, documenting role definitions.
- Security: access policy design, periodic audits, approval authority for elevated privileges.
- Team leads: approve role assignments and periodic access reviews for their team.

Key policies
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum permissions required for the job. Permanent admin privileges require Security and People Ops approval.
- Just-in-time (JIT) access: where supported, use JIT workflows (duration-limited elevated roles) for sensitive operations.
- MFA required: MFA enforced for all accounts with production access.
- Service accounts: must be named using the standard prefix svc-<team>-<purpose> and be registered in the service account inventory.

Onboarding / role change / offboarding process (summary)
1. Request: Manager fills the Access Request form (internal template link below) specifying role, systems, and duration.
2. Approval: Team lead approves; if production/admin access, Security approval required.
3. Provisioning: IT/Cloud Ops provisions accounts following naming and tagging conventions.
4. Verification: New user connects and verifies access within 48 hours.
5. Offboarding: Manager triggers Offboard playbook; all active sessions and API keys are revoked within 4 hours of termination.

Access review cadence
- Quarterly: team leads run access reviews against the access registry.
- Annual: Security performs a full audit of admin accounts and privileged roles.

Exceptions and emergency access
- Exceptions require a short justification and an expiration date; Security tracks exceptions in the risk register.
- Emergency access (e.g., P0 incident) uses the Emergency Access runbook; all emergency sessions are logged and reviewed post-incident.

2) Change management

Purpose
- Reduce risk to production systems while enabling iterative delivery.

Scope
- Applies to infra changes (cloud, network), critical runtime configuration (serving runtime), and any change with potential to impact customer-facing SLAs.

Change categories
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine infra scaling). No CAB required; documented in the change log.
- Minor change: requires peer review and automated test verification.
- Major/change with customer impact: requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval, rollout plan, and rollback plan.

Process summary
1. Submit change request (Change Request form) including impact, owners, rollback plan, monitoring plan, and scheduled window.
2. Automated checks: CI/CD must pass predefined tests; infra linting and policy checks must be green.
3. Approvals: Minor changes — team lead; Major changes — CAB (People Ops, Security, SRE, Product).
4. Implementation: follow runbook, coordinate with oncall where applicable.
5. Post-change verification: health checks for 60 minutes, and a short post-change report posted to the change log.

SLOs and guardrails
- No unapproved changes during 9pm–6am PT unless emergency.
- Rollback plan required for all Major changes.
- Post-change incident rate threshold: if errors exceed 0.5% of baseline request volume in the 60-minute verification window, trigger rollback.

3) Data management

Purpose
- Protect customer and company data, enforce retention, and enable secure collaboration.

Scope
- Covers structured data (databases), object stores, logs, analytics, and PII/sensitive data.

Ownership & roles
- Data Owners (per dataset): set classification, retention, and sharing policy.
- Data Stewards: implement policies and ensure compliance.
- Security: encryption, access control enforcement, incident response.

Classification and handling
- Classifications: public, internal, restricted, confidential.
- Restricted/confidential data: must be stored encrypted at rest and in transit, accessible only on a need-to-know basis, and require approval for external sharing.

Retention and deletion
- Default logs/metrics: retained 90 days in hot storage, 365 days in cold storage.
- Backups: database backups kept 30 days for transactional stores, archived snapshots retained per Data Owner schedule.
- Data deletion: submit Data Deletion Request form; Security and Data Owner approve.

Data sharing and exports
- Internal exports require a business justification and Data Owner approval.
- External sharing (including third-party analytics vendors) requires vendor DPIA and Security approval.

Privacy & compliance
- Follow region-specific requirements for data residency. For regulated customers, Private deployments require contractual controls; consult Legal.

4) Procurement and expenses

Purpose
- Standardize procurement for predictable spend, vendor review, and policy compliance.

Roles & thresholds
- Individual contributor approvals: expenses <= $500 (manager approval).
- Manager approvals: $500 < spend <= $5,000.
- Director approvals: $5,000 < spend <= $50,000.
- VP/Finance approvals: spend > $50,000 and contract terms.

Procurement process (summary)
1. Raise Purchase Request using the procurement template with line item details and justification.
2. Procurement team evaluates vendors for compliance, pricing, and existing contracts.
3. Finance issues PO or card setup; Legal reviews contracts over $50k or involving sensitive data.
4. Receipt and reconciliation: submit receipts and expense forms within 30 days.

Expense policy highlights
- Per diem and travel reimbursements follow the Travel policy section below.
- Company card usage: employees must not share card numbers; transactions are subject to audit.
- Personal purchases: explicitly disallowed unless pre-approved and correctly coded as a reimbursable expense.

5) Vendor management

Purpose
- Ensure vendor risk is identified, contractual obligations are tracked, and vendor performance is monitored.

Vendor lifecycle
- Selection: Procurement evaluates vendors for cost, SLA, security posture, and compliance.
- Onboarding: Security performs initial vendor security questionnaire (VSA) and DPIA if handling data.
- Contracting: Legal drafts/approves terms; Finance records contract term and renewal dates.
- Monitoring: Vendor owner provides quarterly performance reviews; Security refreshes risk assessment annually.
- Offboarding: Decommission integrations, revoke credentials, and confirm secure data deletion.

Security & contractual controls
- Standard clauses: data processing addendum (DPA), right-to-audit, breach notification timelines, and liability caps.
- Higher-risk vendors: require SOC2 or equivalent evidence and may require an on-site assessment.

6) Travel policy

Purpose
- Provide safe and predictable travel processes that balance cost control and employee wellbeing.

Booking and approvals
- Domestic travel: Manager approval required for travel > $250.
- International travel: Manager and People Ops approval required; travel registry entry mandatory.
- Preferred vendors and corporate rates: use company travel portal where available.

Per diem and reimbursements
- Meals: per diem allowances vary by city; use the expense template to claim actuals if above per diem with receipts.
- Lodging: book reasonably priced accommodations; executives should avoid luxury unless pre-approved.

Safety and incident reporting
- Register travel in the Travel Registry for international trips.
- In case of emergency while traveling, contact Global Security and file an incident report to People Ops within 24 hours.

7) Internal templates and forms

This section links to the canonical templates used by the processes above. All templates are stored in the company templates library (confluence template page). Common templates: 
- Access Request form (template link: /confluence/templates/access-request)
- Offboarding checklist (/confluence/templates/offboard-checklist)
- Change Request form (/confluence/templates/change-request)
- Procurement/Purchase Request template (/confluence/templates/purchase-request)
- Vendor Security Assessment (VSA) and DPIA template (/confluence/templates/vsa-dpia)
- Travel Authorization and Expense template (/confluence/templates/travel-expense)
- Post-Change Report template (/confluence/templates/post-change-report)

Template governance
- Templates are owned by People Ops or the process owner noted in the template header. Suggested updates should be submitted as a PR to the templates repo or via the Template Update Request form.

Appendices
- Escalation contacts: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai), Security (security@redwood.ai), Procurement (procurement@redwood.ai).
- Key SLAs: offboard revocation target = 4 hours, emergency access review post-incident = 72 hours, access request turnaround = 48 hours.
- Audit schedule: quarterly access reviews, annual vendor security assessments, annual retention policy review.

Change log
- 2026-03-04: Document created by Sofia Ramirez (People Ops).
- 2026-03-20: Updated with procurement thresholds and travel booking guidance; reviewers: Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair, Daniel Kim.

How to use this document
- Follow the checklists and templates referenced above. For anything not covered, open a request with People Ops or file a policy exception via the Exception Request workflow.

End of document.
